newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates end easier at 23.0625 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates end easier at 23.0625 pct.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interbank rates ended almost half a percentage point lower on Monday, but traders said current levels are still relatively high due to expectations of a repo rate cut.
"Despite official statements over the weekend, the market still feels there is room for one or two repo rate cuts," said Sabdor Tolonics of Commerzbank.
National Bank Chairman Gyorgy Suranyi said on Friday the bank would resist pressure for a sharp drop in interest rates even though it sees inflation continuing to decline steadily.
The benchmark one-week reverse repo rate stands at 21 percent and was last reduced by 0.5 percent on February 17.
Year-on-year inflation was 18.9 percent in January and 18.8 percent in February.

On Monday, overnight rates closed at 23.0625 percent, down from Friday's 23.50 percent and traders said the aftereffect of the March 20 tax payments and two major players taking up money were the other two factors that kept rates relatively high.
